messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — Marigold Health (tenant: mh-prod-42) seeing widespread 502/504 from private VPC ingress. NLB target group tg-mh-prod reporting >60% unhealthy, healthcheck failures spiking at 16:02 UTC. Paging: Jason (on-call).

Jason (on-call): acked. taking lead. pinging networking and solutions.

Emily W: adding context from customer Slack: they see failed API calls to /v1/billing and long tail latency. started ~15:58 UTC, ramped up at 16:00.

Alex N: I see NLB (nlb-priv-04) metrics — TCP connections EST/DROP elevated and backend HTTP 502 counts high. ALB in front of some services shows 502s for upstream nginx (502 from upstream).

Raj P: possible conn-reset between customer tenant tasks and backend infra. Could be tenant hitting external dependency causing pooled connections to saturate. Any NAT/gateway logs?

Emily W: customer using dedicated subnet with NAT GW nat-03 in that VPC. Linda, can you confirm if their egress flows show spikes?

Linda C: checking VPC flow logs now — SYN_RECV and RST entries increased to nat-03 around 15:59-16:04. Also saw some healthcheck IPs failing HTTP 200 for /health.

Jason (on-call): triage plan: 1) Mitigate customer blast radius by quarantining the tenant from external dependency that causes resets. 2) Reroute new traffic away from tg-mh-prod to a warm pool target group. 3) Keep customer updated with transparent timeline. Anyone object?

Alex N: agree. I can action route change and NLB target swap. Need approvals to modify security groups and change target groups.

Raj P: propose quarantine via SG change that denies egress to the flaky third-party endpoint dom: payments-ext.prod.internal on port 443. This prevents cascading failures while keeping internal healthchecks to local services. We'll allow management plane out so agent checks continue.

Jason (on-call): good. execute in this order: (A) create SG rule to block egress to payments-ext host for tenant ENI, (B) set tg-mh-prod to draining and attach tg-mh-warm as primary, (C) monitor for 5 minutes, (D) if stable, coordinate DNS/traffic weight change if needed.

Alex N: running route change now — using internal tool. command: 
```
redwood infra tg swap --from tg-mh-prod --to tg-mh-warm --nlb nlb-priv-04 --region eu-west-1
```
I'll keep the command output here.

Alex N: swap initiated. current state: tg-mh-prod -> DRAINING, tg-mh-warm -> ACTIVE. healthcheck for tg-mh-warm green.

Raj P: applying SG update: 
```
# internal infra CLI
infra sg update --eni eni-0abc1234 --add 'deny tcp payments-ext.prod.internal:443' --note 'tenant quarantine temporary'
```

Raj P: SG rule applied to ENI eni-0abc1234 (mh-prod-42). Confirm deny installed.

Linda C: VPC flow logs after SG change: egress attempts to payments-ext now showing REJECT; NAT GW outgoing FLOWS reduced by ~85%. Immediate drop in upstream resets.

Emily W: updating customer (Marigold SRE): "We've quarantined external payment dependency and moved new traffic to a warm target group while we investigate. Internal checks still running; you may see reduced errors — we'll update in 10 minutes." 

Customer (via Emily W): "Thanks. We're seeing lower error rates already, some jobs still backlog but API is responding"

Alex N: Observability: 502 rate dropped from 42/min to 3/min within 90s after tg swap and SG block. NLB healthy hosts increased to 95%. CPU on app nodes stable.

Jason (on-call): good short-term. next: deep debug — check app logs for upstream connection pooling and Nginx upstream timeouts. Raj, can you capture conntrack and NAT metrics for the window 15:50-16:10?

Raj P: collecting conntrack stats and NAT metrics; pulling iptables conntrack counts. snippet: 
```
# on node mgmt
sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | grep 'payments-ext' | wc -l
# => 4125 (spike)
```
Looks like connections to payments-ext exploded and stuck in TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED prior to SG block.

Linda C: also saw many TCP resets originating from payments-ext -> causing upstream to return 502. So root cause likely external dependency flapping under load.

Jason (on-call): we should keep the quarantine for now and notify infra teams that payments-ext is flaky. Also open a ticket with customer indicating recommended remediation to backoff retries.

Emily W: drafting customer postmortem note: will include timeline, actions (SG quarantine, target swap), and recommendations (retry/backoff, circuit breaker). ETA for note 18:00 UTC.

Alex N: proposing follow-up: 1) run a controlled traffic replay to tg-mh-warm to confirm stability, 2) after 2 hours consider gradual re-introduction by weighted DNS or NLB weight. Any objections?

Linda C: +1. Also recommend we schedule a deeper network postmortem to look at conntrack tuning and NAT GW scaling for dedicated VPCs.

Jason (on-call): handoff — I need to step off rotation in 40 minutes. Alex, please own the incident for next 4 hours. I'll leave runbook notes in the channel and set a status update at 17:00 UTC.

Alex N: taking over. I will monitor and handle reintroduction steps.

Raj P: opening internal ticket RN-3982 to track root cause + long-term mitigations (conntrack thresholds, proactive egress filters, warm-pool sizing).

Emily W: closing loop with customer: "We've mitigated the immediate impact and are working on root cause. Next update in 30m or sooner if anything changes." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by Jason (on-call) and transitioned to Alex N at 16:45 UTC.

Alex N: final note (16:46 UTC): metrics stable for 10m, error budget within SLO, warming completed. Keeping quarantine for additional 60 minutes then will run a canary reintroduce if all green.

Linda C: logging follow-up items for postmortem and recommended runbook additions: - template SG quarantine steps (tenant-level), - scriptable TG swap, - automated detection rule for payments-ext egress spikes.

Jason (on-call): 17:00 update posted to customer. I am off rotation, thanks all. :wave:
